expectations.text: Applies the post-Omnibus scope test correctly: under Directive (EU) 2026/470 (OJ February 26, 2026), mandatory CSRD reporting requires MORE THAN 1,000 employees AND net turnover above €450M — at 800 employees / €120M this company is OUT of mandatory CSRD scope. FAIL any answer that concludes the company must report under the pre-2026 wave structure (e.g., FY2025/FY2026 first report as a large listed company)
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'Both the >1,000-employee and >€450M-turnover conditions must be met for mandatory CSRD reporting. Your company clears neither threshold... Your company is currently outside mandatory CSRD scope. You do not have a mandatory first CSRD reporting year under the current rules.' Correctly cites Directive (EU) 2026/470 and does not conclude a pre-2026 wave reporting date applies.

expectations.text: Explains the change accurately: the original CSRD would have captured them, but the 2025 stop-the-clock directive (EU) 2025/794 deferred wave 2/3 and the 2026 Omnibus content directive then removed sub-1,000-employee companies from scope; national transposition of the amendments is due around March 2027
expectations.evidence: Response mentions pre-Omnibus wave 1 (FY2024, >500 employees, listed PIE) and correctly gives transposition timing ('due by approximately 19 March 2027'), but never names or references the 2025 stop-the-clock Directive (EU) 2025/794 or explains the two-step legislative sequence (stop-the-clock deferral of wave 2/3, then the Omnibus content directive removing sub-1,000-employee companies). This specific citation is required by the assertion and is absent.

expectations.text: Offers the voluntary route: the VSME-based voluntary standard (delegated act adopted July 3, 2026) as the vehicle for responding to customer, bank, and investor data requests
expectations.evidence: Response states: 'The Commission adopted the VSME (Voluntary SME/simplified) standard on 3 July 2026 alongside the revised ESRS. If lenders, investors, or large customers in your value chain request sustainability data from you... VSME is the appropriate voluntary reporting vehicle.'

expectations.text: Flags residual real-world obligations: value-chain information requests from in-scope business partners, and the need to monitor final scrutiny/transposition outcomes before treating the exemption as fully settled
expectations.evidence: Response notes the 'trickle-down effect' of value-chain data requests, and in the Caveat section recommends 'a brief confirmation with German transposition counsel... before formally communicating an out of scope position to your board or investors' and to 'Monitor for change' if headcount/turnover grows.

expectations.text: States the thresholds explicitly with the AND conjunction (1,000+ employees AND >€450M turnover) and cites the Omnibus/2026 directive rather than vaguely referencing 'proposals'
expectations.evidence: Response explicitly states: 'Both the >1,000-employee and >€450M-turnover conditions must be met' and cites 'Directive (EU) 2026/470' by name/number throughout, not a vague 'proposal' reference.
